text:
Sarah (CS): Hey team — linking post-incident follow-up here. Customer X (enterprise dedicated) just asked for a short RCA and whether we'll be offering an SLA credit. Can we draft the external note + internal timeline and action items?

IncidentBot: [INCIDENT] 1779123456 · Resolved · Service degradation affecting hosted generation. Severity: P2. Pager routed to @Mike (on-call).

Mike (on-call): Quick timeline from the run: detected at ~03:12 UTC by autoscaler alarms, traffic throttled at ~03:16, mitigations started 03:18 (scaled to spare capacity), partial recovery 03:34, full recovery 03:41 after rollback of the rolling quantized model variant. Root cause suspected during initial triage: rollout + autoscaler interaction.

Alex (Eng): Confirming — root cause: race between the new quantized model variant initialization path and the autoscaler cooldown logic. When the model process crashed during cold start, the autoscaler interpreted it as sustained low utilization and started deprovisioning a node; that removed capacity while other requests still retried, amplifying latency and 429s. Reverted the rollout at 03:20 which stabilized things; full cleanup finished by 03:41.

Jess (PM): Thanks. CS: do we have a short external-friendly summary and a proposed compensation language? Also need to know whether any customer data or requests were dropped (customer asks that explicitly).

Sarah (CS): Customer asked: Did any requests fail permanently? Any data loss? They want estimated affected percentage of requests and whether dedicated workloads were impacted differently.

Alex (Eng): No persisted data loss. Some in-flight requests got 429/timeout and were retried by clients; our logs show ~0.7% of requests in their org received an error response during the window 03:12–03:41. Dedicated tenants: two Dedicated clusters that had the quantized variant enabled saw higher error rates (2.8% and 1.9%) because they were on the same node pool that experienced the deprovision. We're compiling per-tenant exact counts.

Mike (on-call): Mitigation steps we executed:
- rolled back the quantized model variant (03:20)
- increased autoscaler cooldown from 30s -> 180s as hotfix (03:25)
- added temporary routing to pre-warmed pool for the tenant (03:28)
- verified recovery and scaled nodes back down (03:41)

Alex (Eng): Long-term fixes proposed:
1) Add atomic startup handshake for model variants so autoscaler only counts healthy instances.
2) Fix autoscaler bug where exit code X triggers deprovision incorrectly.
3) Add canary gating for quantized rollouts with staged traffic ramps.
4) Add tenant-level alerting for error rate >0.5% sustained for 5m.

Sarah (CS): Draft external status page blurb (please edit for tone).

```
INCIDENT: Service degradation for text generation — Resolved
Time window: 2026-03-12 03:12 UTC -> 2026-03-12 03:41 UTC
Summary: A model rollout interaction with our autoscaling subsystem caused transient increased error rates for a subset of customers. We reverted the rollout and applied mitigations which restored service.
Impact: Some requests received error responses (429/timeout). No persisted data loss. Affected customers may have experienced degraded performance or failed requests during the window.
Next steps: Engineering has implemented a short-term autoscaler cooldown change and will deploy a targeted fix to prevent this class of issue. We will provide a follow-up with additional details and prevention steps.
```

Jess (PM): That looks good — maybe add an explicit line offering to share per-tenant logs if they want.

Sarah (CS): Draft customer email (short, empathetic). Please adapt language: 

```
Hi <Customer X contact>,

We wanted to follow up about the service disruption you experienced on 2026-03-12 between 03:12–03:41 UTC. During that time a new model variant rollout triggered an interaction with our autoscaling system which caused elevated error rates for some of your requests.

What we did: We reverted the rollout, increased autoscaler cooldown, and routed affected traffic to a pre-warmed pool to restore service.

Impact: We observed ~0.7% of your requests returned errors during the window. There was no persisted data loss.

Next steps: Engineering will deploy a permanent fix and add extra canary gating to future rollouts. We'll update you once the fix is live.

If you'd like, we can provide a per-request log export for your team, and discuss SLA credit options.

Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Sarah and the Redwood team
```

Mike (on-call): Small nit — suggest we avoid the raw percent in the first outreach, or give context (e.g., 0.7% of requests during the window = ~X requests). Some customers react strongly to percentages without denominators.

Sarah (CS): Good point. We'll include both: percent + absolute count. Alex — can you confirm counts for Customer X?

Alex (Eng): Pulling the tenant query now. Quick numbers: ~860k requests total in the window for Customer X; ~6,020 error responses (~0.7%). For the two Dedicated clusters: cluster A: 2,100 errors of 75k requests (2.8%), cluster B: 1,420 errors of 74k requests (1.9%). I'll add these to the internal appendix doc: https://internal.redwood/reports/1779123456-incident (internal link).

Jess (PM): On SLA credit — our policy: for P2 sustained impact with measurable error rate above threshold we usually offer a pro-rated credit. Ops/finance approval required. Sarah, please propose a credit amount (e.g., 10% of monthly invoice?) and we'll route to finance.

Sarah (CS): Planning to propose 10% for March billing as a starting point, unless finance pushes back. Also asking whether we should proactively notify all Dedicated customers with the quantized variant enabled. Thoughts?

Mike (on-call): Yes, proactively notify Dedicated customers on that rollout path — they were the most affected and we should be transparent.

Alex (Eng): Technical follow-ups that need owners:
- e2e test for startup handshake (owner: @Alex (Eng))
- autoscaler exit-code fix (owner: @Mike (on-call) + @EngInfra)
- rollout canary gating (owner: @Jess (PM) + @EngRuntime)

Sarah (CS): Action list for CS:
- Prepare external email + status page (owner: @Sarah (CS))
- Prepare per-tenant impact reports (owner: @Alex (Eng))
- Draft SLA credit proposal (owner: @Sarah (CS))
- Coordinate Dedicated-customer proactive outreach (owner: @Olivia (Customer) + @Sarah (CS))

Sarah (CS): I'll send the external email after Alex confirms counts and after we agree on credit amount. Please ack if you own an action item. :white_check_mark:

Alex (Eng): Ack on counts + internal doc.

Mike (on-call): Ack on autoscaler work; will open ticket and link here.

Jess (PM): Ack on canary gating; will schedule follow-up with runtime team.

Olivia (Customer): I'll coordinate outreach to Dedicated customers and will use a slightly gentler tone for enterprise contacts. Will also collect any customer asks to route to engineering.

Sarah (CS): Thanks. One more note — legal/compliance asking whether any contractual notification window was missed. We have 72 hours SLA for incident notifications on Dedicated contracts. We're within that (this is the initial follow-up). If finance/legal want different language we can iterate.

IncidentBot: Reminder: Create post-incident ticket and attach runbook checklist.

Sarah (CS): OK — I will convert this thread into the external note and share a draft for review by 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC. If anyone needs to escalate the credit amount or needs wording changes, ping me directly.

Mike (on-call): I'll drop the autoscaler ticket link here when created: https://internal.redwood/tickets/INC-22480

Alex (Eng): Pls add "add tenant error-rate alert" to INC-22480 as subtask.

Sarah (CS): Great, thanks team. Closing the thread once the email + status update are sent. :pray:
